content.text:
What makes the ant so amazing?

Small but strong, the ant is a social insect that lives together around a queen ant. It's the ultimate teamwork insect — everyone joins forces to accomplish big things!
content.caption: The insect of teamwork

content.alt: Ant - Nature and science facts about the ant
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the ant

A worker ant is strong enough to easily carry loads many times its own body weight. Using the antennae on its head, it follows a scent (pheromone) trail and tells its fellow ants where food is. Ants build an ant nest of many rooms and tunnels underground, and they divide the roles — caring for the eggs, gathering food, and guarding the nest.

content.text:
Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Watch ants marching in a line on the ground and talk about how "they're following a scent trail." Leaving a small bit of food and watching the ants gather lets your child see teamwork firsthand.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How does an ant tell others where food is?
A. It follows a scent (pheromone) trail with the antennae on its head and shows that trail to its fellow ants too.

Q. How strong is an ant?
A. It's strong enough to easily carry loads many times its own body weight.

Q. How can we observe it at home?
A. Watch ants marching in a line, and leave a small bit of food to watch them gather.
